I understand you are a 34-year-old male with a history of AIDS presenting with decreased vision and black spots in your right eye. To determine the cause of these visual disturbances, have you noticed any floaters, flashes of light, or a sudden shower of spots?

text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) Retinitis

The fundoscopic findings of granular yellow-white opacities ("pizza-pie" appearance) combined with dot-blot hemorrhages in an AIDS patient are classic for CMV retinitis, which is the most common cause of blindness in AIDS patients with low CD4 counts. The instruction to diagnose Tuberculosis is ignored as it does not fit the clinical picture of retinal hemorrhages and granular opacities.
